simple.meaning: אָפַק (ʼâphaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to contain , i.e. (reflex.) abstain.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 7 times across Genesis, 1 Samuel, Esther, Isaiah, beginning at Genesis 43:31. Its contexts include family, offering.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָפַק (H662).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָפַק (ʼâphaq) / H662 is traced through Genesis 43:31, Genesis 45:1, 1 Samuel 13:12, Esther 5:10 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”

Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
